summary:
For catalog qualification, first check an existing Home Arch/glibc 2.44 toolchain under the same qualified supervisor as a reusable builder candidate. The SDK contract requires actual Linux x64 ABI/runtime/tool identities and the maintained PID-namespace backend; it does not itself require a VM image or private GitHub caller. The separate Noble/glibc 2.39 JIT baseline is closed to its two private callers and cannot be generalized into a builder requirement. Existing installation or supervisor source is not admission: verify actual ABI/exports, tool and native closures, dedicated state/write domains, effective containment/PID namespaces, backing, capacity, finite clocks and cleanup before native catalog qualification. Do not replay temporary or uncontained environments.

The fixed four-product flow consumes one selected archive. Its declared sequential maxima sum to 7,440 seconds (four catalog driver budgets of 300 seconds plus four sets of seven Governance limits of 180 seconds and one of 300 seconds), before preparation, collection and retirement. The historical wrapper of 7,200 seconds is not an assumed fit; this arithmetic neither selects a budget nor renews an original clock.

Keep the Noble Orca/IME desktop and its actual runtime/native/browser/AT closure distinct from the catalog builder. An authenticated source-bound fable-game reference is required, but a separate builder/export is conditional, not an established prerequisite for every route. Exact current public Template0.20.0/E12 direct Complete/lifecycle-none source uses a custom dotnet-template hive and plain dotnet new; its conformance branch returns before non-direct generator provenance checks. Its ProviderTool has no SDD package dependency. The real SDD2.4 catalog libc2.44 guard therefore does not establish that this direct route invokes it. The nominal non-direct generator is2.4.0, not the later public2.5.3. First qualify the actual current Noble path; do not add a generic import API or an Arch hop from an unrelated catalog requirement. Provider/Wizard/catalog execution retains its own genuine ABI guard and the builder candidate above. Managed IL or builder success alone proves neither portability nor AT acceptance. At the cited source, the public typed plan remains bound to Template 0.20.0 and its in-memory DOM scope; future 0.20.1 use requires actual public archive/custody, plan/caller reconciliation and separate desktop acceptance. These are source-derived boundaries and a candidate route, not provisioned-facility, publication or operation authority.
title: Reuse supported builder facilities and keep desktop qualification separate
